content: The type of blast chillers installed in each food preparation area is determined by the specific concept or menu, the operational requirements necessary to meet that menu, and the volume of food that requires cooling. Utility sinks are provided in all meat, fish, and vegetable preparation rooms, as well as in cold pantries or garde mangers, and in any other areas where personnel wash or soak food. Additionally, an automatic vegetable washing machine may be used in vegetable preparation rooms alongside the food preparation utility sinks. Food storage areas include storage cabinets, shelves, or racks for food products and equipment. These are located in food storage, preparation, and service areas, including bars and pantries. Fixed or portable tables, carts, or pallets are placed in areas where food or ice is dispensed from cooking equipment, such as soup kettles, steamers, braising pans, tilting pans, or ice storage bins. Storage for large utensils must include a cabinet or rack for items such as ladles, paddles, whisks, and spatulas. Additionally, vertical storage must be provided for cutting boards. Deck drains, scuppers, and sinks must be appropriately sized to prevent spillage and overflow onto adjacent deck surfaces. Sufficient deck drainage must be provided, and deck and scupper drain lines in all food service and warewashing areas must be designed to prevent liquids from pooling on the decks. Deck sinks must not be used as substitutes for deck drains. Cross-drain connections must be installed to prevent pooling and spillage from scuppers when the vessel is listing. If a non-removable coaming is provided around deck drains, the junction with the deck must be coved. Integral coving is not required. Ramps installed over thresholds must be easily removable or sealed in place. They should be sloped for easy trolley roll-in and roll-out and must be strong enough to maintain their shape. If ramps over scupper covers are part of the scupper system, they must be constructed of smooth, durable, and easily cleanable materials. The installation of drain lines carrying black water or other liquid wastes directly overhead or horizontally through spaces used for food preparation or storage (including bars, deck pantries, and buffet counters) should be minimized. If unavoidable, steel piping must be sleeve-welded or butt-welded, and plastic piping must be heat-fused or chemically welded. For scupper lines, factory-assembled transition fittings for steel-to-plastic pipes are allowed if manufactured per ASTM F1973 or equivalent standards. Push-fit or press-fit piping must not be used in these areas. Handwashing stations in food areas must be supplied with hot and cold potable water. The water temperature must be maintained between 38°C (100°F) and 49°C (120°F) using a mixing valve or combination faucet. Handwashing sinks in food areas must be constructed of stainless steel. In food service areas and bars, sinks may also be made of a similar smooth, durable material. Handwashing stations must include a soap dispenser, paper towel dispenser, corrosion-resistant waste receptacle, and, where necessary, splash panels to protect adjoining equipment, clean utensils, food storage, or food preparation surfaces. If attached to the bulkhead, soap dispensers, paper towel dispensers, and waste receptacles must be permanently sealed or removable for cleaning. Air hand dryers are not permitted. Soap and paper towel dispensers must not be installed over adjoining equipment, clean utensil storage, food storage, food preparation surfaces, bar counters, or water fountains. For multi-station sinks, a soap dispenser must be within 380 millimeters (15 inches) of each faucet, and a paper towel dispenser must be within 760 millimeters (30 inches) of each faucet. Paper towel dispensers must be installed at least 450 millimeters (18 inches) above the deck, as measured from the lower edge of the dispenser. Handwashing sinks must be installed at least 750 millimeters (30 inches) above the deck, as measured at the top edge of the basin, to ensure employees do not have to reach excessively to wash their hands. Counter-mounted handwashing sinks must be installed at least 600 millimeters (24 inches) above the deck, as measured at the counter level. The minimum size of the handwashing sink basin must be 300 millimeters (12 inches) in length and 300 millimeters (12 inches) in width. For round basins, the diameter must be at least 300 millimeters (12 inches). Additionally, the minimum distance from the bottom of the water tap to the bottom of the basin must be 200 millimeters (8 inches).
